rows.body_text: At the heart of this process is the flow of raw materials to manufacturers, the distribution of goods to retailers, and the delivery of goods and services to consumers. Along the way, many products are handled by intermediaries who form a link along the supply chain. One example is suppliers, who buy raw materials or manufactured goods from one business and sell them to another business. For example, in Figure 1.8-2 , a supplier buys grain from a farm and sells it to a cereal manufacturer. Similar to suppliers but generally further along in the supply chain are distributors , who typically buy products from manufacturers and sell them to retail stores. In Figure 1.8-2 , a distributor buys cereal from the cereal manufacturer and sells it to grocery stores.
